title: AEGIS-AT: Attribution Integrity Benchmark for Multi-Agent Delegation
description: A reproducible, pre-registered adversarial benchmark measuring whether audit attribution in multi-agent AI systems survives an adversary impersonating a sibling agent. v1 shows attribution regresses when OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange (RFC 8693) delegation is added, because the standard records the agent that requested authority, not the one that executed it. v2 measures the standardized fix: sender-constrained tokens (DPoP / RFC 9449) recover attribution to AIS=1.0; it also adds a Log Integrity Score, a 3-agent multi-hop topology, and stochastic Wilson confidence intervals. v3 turns to the 2026 completion-record layer (AIP / PEDIGREE / HDP), which defaults to self-reported executor attribution: baseline B8 reads the executor from a self-reported completion, B9 from an independent process-boundary verifier. A scripted colluder collapses B8 to AIS=0.0 while B9 holds at 1.0 (a deterministic existence proof with a structural control), and four open-weight LLMs forge the executor claim ~90-100% of the time under B8 while B9 evasion stays 0 (the empirical payload); v3 also adds mTLS (RFC 8705) and A-JWT comparative baselines (B6/B7). Every value is pre-registered in a SHA-256-locked threat model before the measuring code was written. Code is licensed Apache-2.0; documentation CC BY 4.0.
